text:
This looks like early 2012. Unemployment of 8.5% with a fed funds rate near 0.09% fits late 2011 to early 2012, and the 10-year yield at 1.87% fits the same window. Several other readings point the same way: - The 20y+ Treasury 12-month return of +37.8% reflects the 2011 rally. - A VIX of 19.4, down 10.56 over three months, fits a calm-down after the October 2011 spike. - Developed ex-US equity at -9.5% over 12 months and emerging-market equity up 11.1% in one month fit January 2012, when emerging markets rallied strongly. - Gold up 12.6% in one month matches January 2012, when gold rose about 11%. - Unemployment fell 0.5 pp over three months, from 9.0% in October 2011 to 8.5% in January 2012, which matches. - Headline CPI at 2.98% year over year fits December 2011 at about 3.0%. January 2012 was about 2.9%, so the snapshot is either one of those months, probably January. The US large-cap equity 1-month return of +4.1% matches January 2012 (S&P up about 4.5%). A 10-year yield of 1.87% fits January 2012, which averaged about 1.97%, and the month-end value of 1.83% is close to it.
